definitions.explanation: Taking decisive action despite hesitation or fear; making a bold move.

examples.japanese: {思|おも}い{切|き}って{告白|こくはく}した。
{思|おも}い{切|き}って{会社|かいしゃ}を{辞|や}めた。
examples.english: I took the plunge and quit the company.

examples.japanese: {思|おも}い{切|き}って{聞|き}いてみたら、{案外|あんがい}あっさりOKだった。
examples.english: When I boldly asked, they surprisingly agreed easily.

notes:
FORMATION:
{思|おも}い{切|き}る (to make up one's mind) → {思|おも}い{切|き}って (te-form as adverb)

NUANCE:
Implies overcoming hesitation or fear to take action. Often used when doing something one has been putting off or afraid to do.

RELATED FORMS:
・{思|おも}い{切|き}り - to one's heart's content; with all one's might
・{思|おも}い{切|き}った - bold, decisive (adjective use)

COLLOCATIONS:
・{思|おも}い{切|き}って{言|い}う - to speak up boldly
・{思|おも}い{切|き}って{挑戦|ちょうせん}する - to take on a challenge boldly
・{思|おも}い{切|き}った{決断|けつだん} - a bold decision
・{思|おも}い{切|き}った{行動|こうどう} - bold action

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{大胆|だいたん}に - boldly
・{勇気|ゆうき}を{出|だ}して - courageously
